back: The angle measured clockwise from (grid) north to the line joining two places, written with three figures, e.g. 045°.
Add 180° to a bearing below 180°, or subtract 180° from one of 180° or more, e.g. 053° ↔ 233°.
Points 22.5° apart: e.g. NNE 022.5°, ENE 067.5°, ESE 112.5°, SSE 157.5°.
The direction of the vertical grid lines (eastings) on a map; the north used for map bearings.
The angle between grid (or true) north and magnetic north, printed in the map margin; it changes slowly over time.
Grid to magnetic: add the declination. Magnetic to grid: subtract it.
Stand at B (the place after 'from'), draw north there, and measure clockwise to A.
